title: unify-sdks-auth-retries-streaming-ergonomics-and-parity-version-bump
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Unified SDK behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go: consistent auth token refresh and retry/backoff, improved streaming ergonomics (async iterators + event hooks), various parity fixes, and minor version bumps for all SDKs.
description:
Context: customers and internal tooling were exercising three SDKs with subtle differences in auth refresh, retry/backoff, and streaming ergonomics. This caused surprising behavior on transient auth failures and forced consumers to write duplicate wiring. This PR consolidates the behavior across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs, improves ergonomics for streaming responses, and bumps SDK versions for parity.

What I changed (high-level):
- Auth & retries: standardize token refresh hook and default retry/backoff policy. All SDKs now expose the same configurable RetryPolicy (initial_backoff, max_backoff, multiplier, retryable_statuses) and a token refresh callback that will be invoked before retryable requests. Implemented jittered exponential backoff and moved permanent vs transient classification into shared design docs (ENG-3421).
- Streaming ergonomics: unify on an async-iterator style API in Python/TS and a channel/event API in Go that mirrors it. Added on_event hooks for partial messages, metadata, and cancellation, and standardized close/error semantics so user code can rely on same semantics across languages.
- Parity fixes: aligned method names and parameters for create_completion / stream_completion across SDKs, fixed edge cases in metadata propagation and request header handling, and added consistent per-stream timeout handling.
- Version bumps: python 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0, typescript 0.9.5 -> 0.10.0, go v0.8.1 -> v0.9.0.

- Priya Shah: found an edge case where TypeScript browser build dropped partial messages under heavy backpressure; requested a fix and an e2e test.
- Author: pushed a fix that buffers a small event queue in browser builds and added an e2e test using the perf-canary harness.
- Liam O'Connor: approved with one suggestion to make the Go error type more idiomatic; change applied in a follow-up commit.

breaking_change_guidance: No breaking API changes were made intentionally. There are minor signature normalizations (parameter reorder and renamed helpers) documented in docs/sdk-migration.md. Recommend bumping client pinning policy to next minor for compatibility.
